title: Cost of Honesty for Mode Confidence Intervals at a Flat Quartic Density
banked_reason: D-0.5 v3 is sound but letter-tier: the same-density nested-honesty gap is below the field floor; randomized causal transfer adds no new frontier, and a field-tier extension requires new machinery.
gap_reasons: The proposed target is an observed single-density mode with no treatment, potential-outcome, assignment, or causal estimand; the honest_scope expressly disclaims causal transfer, so its causal-stat contribution is letter-tier rather than the required field tier.
Romano1988 Theorem 3.1 and the full class hypotheses of Klemela2005 and Vieu1996 remain uninspected, preventing a supported novelty judgment for the sharp mode-frontier claims.
proof_attempt_summary: Two revisions developed the shrinking-curvature slice package and its uniform construction certificate, but could not clear the Romano/Klemelä/Vieu theorem-level collision. A distinct third version isolated a sound same-density nested-honesty gap: expected length n^(-5/39) under ambient asymmetric honesty versus n^(-1/2) under fixed-neighborhood exact-evenness honesty. It remained letter-tier because it is a single-density noncausal example; randomized armwise transfer adds no new frontier, while an observational or treatment-design extension needs new machinery.
tldr: At one fixed flat symmetric quartic density, how much longer must a confidence interval for its mode be when coverage must hold over a larger six-smooth quartic class instead of a locally even subclass? The proposed pointwise lengths are \(n^{-5/39}\) under ambient honesty and \(n^{-1/2}\) under local-symmetry honesty, giving a penalty of \(n^{29/78}\).
gap: Existing mode estimation and adaptive confidence-interval theorems do not directly evaluate pointwise optimal expected length for this nonlinear mode under the two nested density classes.
fill: Establish both sharp pointwise frontiers through a common class certificate, two testing pairs, and matching honest intervals.
